raw_record.support_text: Significant hepatotoxicity has been reported with the use of tacrine. All patients receiving tacrine should have baseline liver function tests performed, and liver function tests should be followed during weeks 4 through 16. Patients should be alert for symptoms of liver failure, and dosing guidelines are adjusted in response to liver function testing.
raw_record.extra_details: Tacrine (Cognex) is an acridine-derivative cholinesterase inhibitor FDA-approved in 1995 for Alzheimer's disease. In double-blind placebo-controlled trials, a significant percentage of patients, especially those at higher doses, withdrew because of intolerable hepatotoxicity and cholinergic side effects. Liver function test monitoring is recommended from weeks 4 through 16 with baseline testing; dosing is adjusted based on LFT results, and tacrine should be used with caution in hepatic insufficiency. Oral dosing divided into initial (10 mg four times daily for 4 weeks), titration up to maximum 160 mg total per day.

raw_record.support_text: The authors attribute prolonged cholestasis in their patient to amitriptyline based on: absence of biliary tract disease (normal retrograde cholangiography and ultrasound), no serologic or circumstantial evidence of viral hepatitis, negative serum antitissue antibodies, and discontinuation of other drugs 2 weeks before jaundice onset without reported hepatotoxicity. The clinical presentation (jaundice after 5 weeks of amitriptyline, transient eosinophilia, initial centrilobular cholestasis) resembled previously reported amitriptyline-induced acute cholestatic hepatitis. Despite stopping amitriptyline, cholestasis was markedly protracted, with pruritus and jaundice lasting 19 and 20 months and abnormal liver tests persisting at 2 years; three liver biopsies showed progression from centrilobular cholestasis to portal inflammation, ductular proliferation, moderate fibrosis, and partial disappearance of interlobular bile ducts.
raw_record.extra_details: Single patient case report. Jaundice onset 5 weeks after starting amitriptyline, accompanied by transient blood eosinophilia. Outcome remarkable for protracted cholestasis: pruritus for 19 months and jaundice for 20 months; liver tests still abnormal 2 years after jaundice onset. Three serial liver biopsies documented initial centrilobular cholestasis progressing to portal inflammatory infiltration, ductular proliferation, moderate fibrosis, and partial loss of interlobular bile ducts. Competing causes excluded (no biliary disease, no viral hepatitis, negative antitissue antibodies). Hepatitis suggested to be immunoallergic; a reactive-metabolite/immune mechanism analogous to imipramine/amineptine was hypothesized. Debrisoquine/dextromethorphan oxidation phenotyping showed an extensive metabolizer phenotype (metabolic ratio 0.009), indicating amitriptyline hydroxylation was not deficient.

raw_record.support_text: In a 56-year-old woman taking citalopram (Cipramil) 20 mg/d for 3 weeks who presented with weakness, jaundice, and hepatomegaly, an acute hepatic injury developed while on treatment. Authors state the causal association with citalopram can be established based on a temporal relationship between drug administration and hepatic injury that was subsequently histologically confirmed, and the patient rapidly improved after the drug was stopped, with complete normalization of liver tests within 3 months. Histology showed subacute liver dystrophy and liver cell necrosis consistent with drug-induced liver injury.
raw_record.extra_details: 56-year-old woman took citalopram (Cipramil) 20 mg/d for 3 weeks; presented with weakness, asthenia, weight loss, jaundice, mild hepatomegaly; no alcohol or other drugs, no prior liver disease; abdominal ultrasound compatible with acute hepatitis. Elevated bilirubin 11 mg/dL (<1), AST 5.7 µmol/s/L (0.1-0.60), ALT 14.2 µmol/s/L (0.17-0.60), GGT 6.9 µmol/s/L (<1.10); autoantibodies and viral hepatitis screens normal. Liver biopsy consistent with drug-induced liver injury showing subacute liver dystrophy and liver cell necrosis of zones 2 and 3, histologically indistinguishable from acute viral hepatitis. Complete normalization of liver function tests in 3 months after citalopram cessation. Authors note citalopram data sheets only in some countries mention pathological liver function tests, and no recommendation for routine liver monitoring.

raw_record.support_text: The authors report an acute cholestatic syndrome temporally associated with administration of the antiarrhythmic drug propafenone, believing the drug was involved due to a close time relationship between drug administration and onset of liver injury and because rechallenge with propafenone after partial recovery elicited a new significant increase in serum GGT and alkaline phosphatase activities.
raw_record.extra_details: Single-patient case report of acute cholestatic syndrome with jaundice. Onset after 2-4 weeks latency from starting the drug; positive rechallenge after a 2-week course produced a new rise in serum GGT (to 901 IU/L) and alkaline phosphatase (to 615 IU/L). Liver tests reverted to normal within 5 months. Patient also continuously took antidiabetic drugs and enalapril during the whole period. Authors note propafenone hepatotoxicity is very rare (only three prior published cases) and suggest accumulation of toxic hepatic metabolites and enterohepatic recirculation may account for the injury.

raw_record.support_text: The authors critique a prior report attributing liver damage to Nardil (phenelzine) during therapy. They note that one patient had a single 2+ cephalin flocculation test during therapy that was normal on all subsequent tests after the drug was readministered, two other patients' CCF tests returned to normal despite continued drug use, and in another patient a 'hepatoxic effect' was ascribed to Nardil solely on the basis of a single 1+ CCF report. They conclude that interpreting these single abnormal flocculation tests as 'liver damage' in the absence of other clinical or laboratory evidence is not justified.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Authors challenge the previously reported DILI cases; no other laboratory tests (alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, SGOT) were reported in any case, and normal flocculation results occurred despite drug continuation or upon readministration.
raw_record.extra_details: Letter to the editor responding to Kothari's report on 'Toxic and Other Side Effects of Nardil, Phenelzine Sulphate W1544A'. The authors argue cephalin flocculation (CCF) tests reflect plasma protein alterations, are not specific liver tests, and were used in isolation (single 1+ to 2+ results) to claim liver damage/hepatotoxicity, an interpretation they regard as unjustified.

raw_record.support_text: After rechallenging the patient with temozolomide alone for 5 cycles, the paper concluded that the toxic hepatitis was not causally related to TEM treatment alone, i.e., temozolomide as a single agent did not cause the liver injury in this patient.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Explicit negative conclusion applies to this single reported patient; the authors attributed the toxic hepatitis to the concomitant Chinese herbal formula (Bu Zhong Yi Qi Wan) rather than to temozolomide alone.

raw_record.support_text: In this clinical trial of praziquantel vs oxamniquine for schistosomiasis, the post-treatment laboratory work-up failed to demonstrate any relevant abnormality in either treatment group for AST, ALT, and γ-GT. The percentage of liver enzyme results that changed from normal to abnormal after treatment with either drug was low and similar to the percentage of changes in the reverse direction (McNemar test: p > 0.05), indicating no clinically meaningful drug-related liver enzyme change was attributable to either drug.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Assessment in patients with schistosomiasis treated in an efficacy trial; conclusion based on liver enzyme follow-up rather than formal DILI adjudication.
raw_record.extra_details: Patients remained under clinical observation for 24 hours after intake; liver enzymes (AST/SGOT, ALT/SGPT, γ-GT), alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin tested before and 1 day after treatment (53 praziquantel patients), with hepatic enzymes re-tested 1 week afterwards. Enzyme changes from normal to abnormal were low and comparable to reverse changes (McNemar p>0.05).

raw_record.support_text: Ketamine undergoes extensive hepatic metabolism, and although short-term use has been infrequently associated with elevated liver function tests, the paper explicitly states that clinically apparent liver damage has not been reported. Supporting observations include Dundee et al. finding significant liver-function elevations in 14 of 34 patients given 3-4 mg/kg ketamine for anesthesia, and a randomized trial by Noppers et al. in which 3 of 6 patients re-exposed to ketamine 16 days after a 100-hour infusion (mean dose 1813 mg) developed elevations ≥3 times baseline that returned to normal within 3 months. Approximately 10% of individuals receiving high-dose ketamine infusions experience significant liver-enzyme increases, yet no adverse hepatic effects were reported in a 60-patient CRPS RCT (average dose 22 mg/h over ~4.2 days).
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Negative claim pertains specifically to clinically apparent liver damage; isolated elevations in liver enzymes/transaminases are reported but are not characterized as clinically apparent drug-related liver injury.
raw_record.extra_details: Short-term use infrequently associated with elevated liver function tests. Dundee et al.: 14 of 34 patients receiving 3-4 mg/kg ketamine for anesthesia had significant liver-function elevations. Noppers et al. RCT: 3 of 6 patients re-exposed to ketamine 16 days after a 100-hour infusion (max 0.4 mg/kg/h, mean dose 1813 mg) developed ≥3 times baseline liver-enzyme elevations that normalized within 3 months; the other two groups showed no abnormal liver tests. Approximately 10% of high-dose ketamine infusion recipients develop significant liver-enzyme increases. No adverse hepatic effects in a 60-patient CRPS RCT with continuous ketamine infusion (average 22 mg/h, ~4.2 days). The paper concludes there is insufficient evidence supporting routine preinfusion liver testing before IV ketamine in healthy individuals, but suggests case-by-case baseline/postinfusion LFTs for those with liver dysfunction, at risk of hepatotoxicity (e.g., alcohol abusers, chronic hepatitis), or receiving high frequent doses (grade C, low certainty).

raw_record.support_text: The antihypertensive regimen used a stepped care approach with atenolol as first-line treatment, followed by bendrofluazide and nifedipine; the paper states that atenolol and bendrofluazide have not been reported to cause hepatotoxic side effects.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Used as first-line antihypertensive agent in a stepped care regimen; negative only for reported hepatotoxicity, not a systematic assessment.
raw_record.extra_details: Atenolol and bendrofluazide together were stated not to have been reported to cause hepatotoxic side effects; the negative assertion is about the absence of published reports, not a dedicated safety study.

raw_record.support_text: In a study by Romanenko, melatonin was administered subcutaneously to C57BL/6 mice twice a week for 5 months starting at 1.5 months of age; nearly 98% of melatonin-treated mice versus 32% of controls developed leukemia, and mean life span was reduced in the treated group. In a separate 2.5-month experiment, leukemia was detected in 70% of melatonin-treated C57BL/6 mice versus 14% of controls, and in 78% of CC57Br mice versus 38% of controls.

The paper elsewhere reports melatonin inhibiting spontaneous and chemical-induced tumors and being non-mutagenic in the Ames test, with clastogenic activity at high concentration in the COMET assay.

raw_record.support_text: The study found that even after prolonged treatment with azathioprine (AZA), the risk of malignancy in multiple sclerosis patients was similar to that of the general population and did not change with subsequent disease-modifying therapies, with no significant increase in cancer incidence compared with the general population.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: multiple sclerosis patients treated with azathioprine
raw_record.extra_details: Retrospective observational cohort; 494 cases analyzed with 22 cancer incidence events. Cox regression hazard ratios for other DMT treatments (0.217, 95% CI 0.026-1.827, p=0.160) and immunomodulating agents (0.511, 95% CI 0.135-1.937, p=0.323) were non-significant; age at AZA start was significant (HR 1.049, p=0.023, increase in younger age groups requiring further investigation). Small number of tumors precluded conclusions about specific tumor types.

raw_record.support_text: This retrospective study of 644 neuroblastoma patients treated with ¹³¹I-MIBG therapy reported a cumulative 10-year incidence of second malignancy of 14.3%. No dose-dependent increase in SMN risk was found among patients who received more ¹³¹I-MIBG treatments or higher cumulative doses per kilogram.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory population; contribution of ¹³¹I-MIBG to SMN risk is difficult to isolate because patients also received prior external beam radiation, alkylating agents, and autologous stem cell transplant.

raw_record.support_text: Chlorpheniramine, a widely used antihistamine, has tested negative for carcinogenicity in the conventional 2-species 2-yr rodent bioassay and therefore is widely accepted as being a noncarcinogen, but there is some positive evidence of in vitro (BALB/c-3T3) cell transformation potential.
raw_record.extra_details: Widely accepted as a noncarcinogen despite some positive in vitro (BALB/c-3T3) cell transformation evidence (reference 17). Negative for papilloma response in the Tg.AC skin-paint study.

raw_record.support_text: Lithocholic acid is included in the category of 28 non-carcinogens with no or limited evidence of genotoxicity; it is listed in the NTP data base as being negative (N) for, or having no evidence (NE) of, carcinogenicity in both sexes of rats and/or mice.
raw_record.extra_details: CAS 434-13-9; categorized as a rodent non-carcinogen for validation of the in vitro alkaline elution/rat hepatocyte assay.

raw_record.support_text: It has been shown that quercetin transforms cryopreserved embryonal Syrian hamster cells in vitro, but kaempferol does not.
raw_record.evidence_population_or_model: cryopreserved embryonal Syrian hamster cells (Mesocricetus auratus)
raw_record.extra_details: Cited ref 111. Kaempferol did not transform the cells. Kaempferol is mutagenic toward TA98 and TA100; a ubiquitous flavonol.
